study type: Mixed-methods study (provider interviews and surveys, multiple regression analysis)
exposure: Availability of clinical information from an integrated electronic health record system
tubal sterilization requests from office records
new diagnoses generated in the hospital
cohort: The study cohort consists of pregnant individuals receiving care in ambulatory practices and hospitals, whose pregnancy outcomes are analyzed in relation to clinical information availability.
finding: Increased availability of specific clinical information from an integrated electronic health record system is significantly associated with reductions in obstetric trauma, other adverse pregnancy outcomes, preterm births, and low-birth-weight babies.
mod_finding: Better access to prenatal records increases the probability of labor induction and decreases the probability of Cesarean section (C-section).
